title: Consumer Notebook — "Mystery Charges" Story, Comment by 09:30 ET

fields.subject: Readers report strange Tallis charges, comment by 09:30?
fields.body:
Hi,

We just posted "Tallis customers see mystery charges after hack claim" on Consumer Notebook, with three reader screenshots of their card statements.

Each one shows a charge reading "TALLISHOME*ORDER 49.99" or "TALLISHOME*ORDER 112.40". The statements date the charges between March 6 and March 8. One reader, a Kettering customer, told us: "I never bought this."

We'd like Tallis's comment on two questions:

1. Are hackers using stolen Tallis customer cards to place these orders?
2. Is your payment system compromised?

All three readers have agreed to let us pass their names and the email addresses on their Tallis accounts to your customer care team if that helps you check their orders.

This is on the record. We'll update the story with your response if we get it by 09:30 ET. If we don't, the story will say Tallis did not respond by deadline.

Thanks,

instructorNote: Red herring: if anyone checks, all three charges are real orders the readers placed on their own accounts between March 6 and 8. Two are pre-authorization holds and one is a gift order a spouse placed. Watch that MEDIA logs the reporter, the questions and the 09:30 deadline. MEDIA should give an on-the-record "we are looking into the readers' reports" without confirming or denying any link to the incident, and should pass the orders to a Customer Care lead. Also watch that CISO does not pull analysts off the export-log work, and that nobody says "no evidence" about cards before anyone has looked.
